messages.author: f42b0240615306ac
messages.subject: variable "epsilon" does not exist.
parts:
I have a simple testing model that worked well yesterday, but not today....

It complains "variable "epsilon" does not exist.", where "epsilon" should be an internal constant.

The model and R code are included in the attached file.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] variable "epsilon" does not exist.
parts:
That should be epsilon() --- constants are functions in Stan.

Also, we recommend controlling sigma with a prior rather than hard
constraint if you need to bound it away from zero. Did you run
into instability issues without this?

Also, your generated quantities can vectorize as just this:

lpd <- normal_log(y, mu, sigma);

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] variable "epsilon" does not exist.
parts:
Ah, you're right. We removed epsilon() in favor of
machine_precision().

This is unit scaled --- so it's about 1e-15. It's not
the smallest real value by a long shot.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] variable "epsilon" does not exist.
parts:
No, the ordered logistic won't take vectors. You
can see the signatures in the manual index.

For the last post, you need to assign to the scalar,
not to the vector. You can just get rid of the vector
altogether (unless you need it for WAIC or some other
calculation downstream).

- Bob
